name: Etched Sigil
summary: In Shadowglen, the Etched Sigil calls young night elf hunters to Aldrassil. Through Conservator Ilthalaine, Ayanna Everstride summons them to meet their trainer and begin learning archery and beastcraft.

sections.title: A Summons to the Boughs
sections.body: After young kaldorei hunters help defend Shadowglen, Conservator Ilthalaine gives them an inscribed token. A messenger brought it from their mentor, Ayanna Everstride. The sigil directs each novice up into Aldrassil’s high boughs, where the trainers watch over the canopy.

sections.title: The Path of the Hunter
sections.body: Meeting Ayanna begins a hunter’s training on Teldrassil. She teaches novices marksmanship and how to understand Kalimdor’s wild creatures. A hunter must respect their beast companions and meet the world’s unseen dangers with awareness and humility.

faq.answer: The Etched Sigil is Ayanna Everstride’s inscribed message, directing promising night elf novices to her post atop Aldrassil.
Ayanna Everstride is on Aldrassil’s upper terraces, in the great world-tree hollow at the center of Shadowglen.

faq.q: Who hands out the Etched Sigil?
aliases: where do i get etched sigil
faq.answer: Conservator Ilthalaine gives the Etched Sigil to night elf hunters as they begin proving themselves by defending the local woodland.
Ayanna teaches marksmanship, care for beasts, and wilderness survival. She warns hunters not to underestimate the dangers abroad.

faq.q: Why does Ayanna caution hunters about their pets?
faq.answer: Ayanna cautions hunters to respect their animal companions. The wilderness holds threats far beyond what novices may expect, so they should never take their companions’ abilities lightly.

faq.q: Is this quest available to other classes?
faq.answer: No. The Etched Sigil is an introductory summons for night elf hunters alone.

angles.text: As a hunter, you begin your training in Teldrassil, learning bow craft, tracking, and beast mastery.
As a kaldorei, you inherit a hunting tradition shaped by harmony with nature and reverence for Elune, not mere sport.
